What we don't claim

The page nobody writes. These are the limits of what we have built and what we can honestly say about it.

We have not run efficacy studies

We have not measured whether children who use Professor Paws learn more, faster, or better than children who do not. No such study has been run, by us or by anyone else, on this app. Everything on these pages is about method — the reasoning and the sources behind each teaching decision. None of it is a claim about a result, and a citation for a method is not evidence that our version of it works.

Some things have no manipulative, on purpose

Reading comprehension

There is nothing to drag or shade in a reading lesson, and adding one would be decoration. What the evidence describes is talk about text and questions answered with the passage in reach, so that is what the app does: the passage stays on the page — every question is answered with the text in reach, and the help ladder points back INTO it rather than around it.

Times tables practice

The multiplication tile is a typed drill by design. Practice there is about quick recall of facts a child has already been taught with a picture elsewhere, and putting a manipulative on a speed drill would work against the point of it. The teaching version of multiplication — the one with the array — is a different part of the app.

A rejection we currently earn

Our record for Adding, within twenty lists this as something a teaching surface should not do: “counting every counter from one as the taught method, with no route to a derived fact”. The guide names the strategies instruction should be organised around — number combinations, doubles, doubles plus one, and combinations of 10 — and the standard names making ten explicitly. A surface that only ever asks the child to combine and recount teaches the concept and withholds the method, and it does so invisibly, because every answer it produces is correct.

We are naming it here because the record names it, and a record that only ever described what we had already built would not be worth publishing.

Written but not built

A fraction as equal parts of one whole — the record exists and the representation is chosen, but the surface is not in the app yet. The record says so, and so does this page.

What a citation here means, and what it doesn't

A quoted source on these pages means: this is where the representation came from. It does not mean the source studied our app, endorses it, or predicts anything about your child. Curriculum codes are recorded for accuracy about a standard's wording; we never compare a child against a year group or grade, and the app cannot compute such a comparison.
